scope: mu(t), Sigma(t), realized returns, and validation reports for ODE portfolio optimization handoff

extra_mu_candidates.purpose: Reference / baseline mu(t) spectrum so the ODE team can measure how much each signal layer actually contributes. No retraining: all model sources are existing walk-forward predictions on the identical fold grid (leakage-clean, directly comparable).
candidates: mu_logistic_cumulative  (raw floor: no image, no deep model; rank corr -0.007)
mu_cnn_1d_cumulative    (high-Sharpe single CNN; rank corr 0.027, Sharpe 0.521)
mu_lstm_image           (best single model overall; rank corr 0.051)
mu_equal_weight         (null floor: constant signal; rank corr undefined)

prices_note: prices_for_ode.csv contains daily close prices for the 7 ETFs (3580 dates, 2012-01-13 to 2026-04-10). Use for transaction-cost / turnover simulation; the OOS signal grid is the 2880-date subset aligned with mu / Sigma files.

recommended_sigma.reason: Ledoit-Wolf shrunk covariance; condition number median 2409->64, all 176 dates with cond>1e4 removed. With constant gamma, w*=(alpha/2 gamma_0) Sigma^-1 mu so a stable inverse matters.
recommended_sigma.comparison_baseline: 03_sigma_returns/sigma_wide.csv (plain 60-day sample covariance, kept for A/B test)

mu_sharpe_baseline.role: Sharpe-stable baseline from prior ensemble sprint

mu_image_factor_rank.role: Recommended ranking-improved input using full OHLC+MA+Volume image factor PC1

mu_image_factor_strict_rank.role: Conservative robustness input using MA recomputed only within each 60-day image window

mu_image_factor_balanced.role: Secondary image-factor input with smaller Sharpe trade-off than the 4-family add-on

calibration.method: expanding pooled OLS future_return ~ 1 + mu_signal by input_name, with horizon embargo
calibration.default_recommendation: use rank-based mu_signal first; use calibrated mu only if return-scale inputs are required
calibration.note: Rebuilt 2026-05 to be repo-reproducible (build_mu_calibration.py). A horizon embargo was added: a training date s is used to calibrate date t only if index(s) + horizon <= index(t), so no not-yet-realised forward return enters the OLS fit. This shifts the first calibrated date to 2015-10-21 and slightly lowers calibrated rank corr versus the earlier un-embargoed file.

known_limitations.walkforward_embargo: generate_walkforward_folds places train/val/test adjacently with no horizon-day purge gap. The last ~horizon training dates per fold carry future_return labels that overlap the adjacent period (~1-2% of training rows contaminated). All models share the identical fold structure, so absolute OOS metrics may be slightly inflated but lift/CI comparisons are contamination-symmetric and approximately unbiased.
known_limitations.calibration_script_history: The original calibrated file had no reproducing script in the repo; build_mu_calibration.py restores reproducibility and adds the horizon embargo above.
known_limitations.bootstrap_ci_method: The bootstrap CIs reported in the image-factor inputs above and in 04_validation_reports were computed with IID resampling, which ignores the autocorrelation induced by the 20-day overlapping return horizon and therefore understates CI width. A stationary block bootstrap (significance_test.md / bootstrap_significance.py) was run on the ensemble-level comparisons: under the block method, the image-factor lift over the image-enabled baseline is NOT statistically significant (block CI includes 0), although the point estimate stays positive. Only the lift over the rawest no-image baseline survives the block bootstrap. Treat the image-factor lift as a positive but autocorrelation-honest-not-significant trend; the statistically robust gain comes from the image transformation itself.

warnings: future_return is an evaluation target, not an ODE input
Sigma(t) is a rolling historical covariance estimate, not a CNN prediction
image-factor lift is regime-sensitive: lift is NEGATIVE in the 2020-2022 covid-inflation subperiod (mu_image_factor_rank rank-corr lift -0.0148, strict -0.0683); see mu_subperiod_stability_report.md
extra ETF supervised pretraining is a negative robustness result and is not recommended as the main ODE input
selected_mu_input.csv default (mu_image_factor_rank) has the lowest top-k Sharpe (0.3155) among candidates; for Sharpe-priority use compare against mu_sharpe_baseline / mu_rank_baseline
